clue.text: Commend a fine novel or a Milton tale

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new or fresh, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone praises a fine novel, or else a story by the poet John Milton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the definition, sitting beside 'a fine', but it is the anagram signal on COMMEND A FINE. Milton is not the poet but George Milton, one of Steinbeck's two drifters.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinbeck's novella follows George Milton and Lennie, so it is a story with Milton at its centre.

clue.text: Late vicar involved in EU party on the rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the whole built string is turned backwards

parts.note: the European Union, taken as written

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the vicar goes inside the party

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title

explanation.surface: A vicar who joined a pro-European party arrived late as it grew in popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' turns the whole string EU + D(REV)O, giving O-VER-D-UE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something late has passed its due time, which is the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Detective squad about to arrest Self near Greece

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold, so the turned squad holds the other pieces inside it
about means turned round, so the word for a squad is read backwards

parts.note: a team is a squad of players

indicators.note: near places Self right beside Greece in the chain

parts.note: I is the self, the first person
GR is the abbreviation for Greece

explanation.surface: A detective team is about to arrest someone near the Greek border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the squad word, and 'to arrest' holds Self and Greece inside the result. Jules Maigret is Simenon's Paris police inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: Simenon's Inspector Maigret is a famous fictional police detective of Paris.

clue.text: Criminal and mafia leaders cross noble conspirator

indicators.note: the leaders of the three words are their first letters

parts.note: to bridge a river is to cross it

explanation.surface: Gangland bosses cross a conspiring aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes the first letters of 'Criminal and mafia'. Richard, Earl of Cambridge, plots against the king in Shakespeare's Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard, Earl of Cambridge, was executed for plotting against Henry V in the Southampton Plot.

clue.text: Fabulous writer a model sent to Heaven

indicators.note: in a down clue sent skyward means read upwards, so the word for model is turned backwards

parts.note: to model is to pose, as for an artist

explanation.surface: A model has died and gone to Heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent to Heaven' turns POSE into ESOP. 'Fabulous' is used literally: a writer of fables.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek storyteller wrote fables, so he is literally a fable-writing author.

clue.text: Chap with overbite medico copper detained in wing

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a medico

indicators.note: detained in means held inside, so the copper sits inside the wing

parts.note: ala is the Latin word for wing, used in anatomy
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A doctor and a policeman held on a hospital wing deal with a man whose teeth jut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is the chemical element; 'detained in' puts it inside the Latin wing. The overbite is the vampire's fangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoker's vampire count has protruding fangs, a jokey way of describing his bite.

clue.text: Anti-crime organization cut up by flipping old regret

indicators.note: by means beside, so the two parts sit next to each other
flipping turns the pieces over, so old and regret are read backwards together

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upwards, so the word for cut is turned backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A police body is cut to pieces because of some old grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns O + RUE into EURO; 'up' turns LOP into POL.
explanation.definitionFit: The European Union's law-enforcement agency coordinates police work against serious crime.

clue.text: Kessler wrote about those in Operation Crucible?

indicators.note: about can mean in a disordered state, so these letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Kessler wrote a war novel about the men in a military operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operation Crucible' sounds like a war story, but a crucible is a pot for melting metal, so its workers make steel.
explanation.definitionFit: A crucible is a vessel for molten metal, so its operators are foundry hands in a mill.

clue.text: Royal family account with Bendini, Lambert and Locke

definitions.meaning: a nickname for the British monarchy as a family business

definitions.text: account with Bendini, Lambert and Locke
definitions.meaning: Grisham's novel about the law practice Bendini, Lambert and Locke

explanation.surface: The royals keep an account with a firm of lawyers.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm is a business; Grisham's novel and the royals' nickname both use the phrase.

clue.text: "On a — night Prince Lucifer uprose" (George Meredith)

definitions.text: "On a — night Prince Lucifer uprose" (George Meredith)

parts.words: "On a — night Prince Lucifer uprose" (George Meredith)
parts.note: the opening line of Meredith's sonnet Lucifer in Starlight, with the adjective for the night left blank

explanation.definitionFit: The missing word describes a sky full of stars, matching the sonnet's title, Lucifer in Starlight.

clue.text: One who drafted Alfred and Emily signs soldier up

definitions.text: One who drafted Alfred and Emily

indicators.note: up can mean in turmoil or out of order, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A soldier signs up for a draft, writing about two people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drafted' and 'soldier ... up' paint a recruitment scene, but 'drafted' means wrote; 'up' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred and Emily is Lessing's last book, about her parents, so she is its author.

clue.text: Old city toured by dying royal King Lear?

indicators.note: toured by means gone round, so the city is surrounded by the other pieces

parts.note: the end is death, the state of dying
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a royal
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city is visited by a dying king, as in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toured by' puts the ancient city inside the dying royal. The question mark marks Lear as an example: he suffers through his ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear bears storm, madness and grief, so he is one who suffers and survives hardship.

clue.text: More like The Whale in best review of theatre

parts.note: a plum job or role is the best one

indicators.note: review read as re-view, looking again from the other way, so the word for theatre is turned backwards

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

explanation.surface: The Whale gets the best review the theatre has given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review of' turns REP into PER. The Whale is a play and film about a very fat man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whale centres on a severely obese man, so fatter is to be more like it.

clue.text: Police in America on the tail of Welsh grass

indicators.note: on the tail of means following behind, so the police word comes after Welsh

parts.note: the heat is American slang for the police

explanation.surface: American police are chasing a Welsh informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like British slang for an informer, but it is the cereal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal crops are members of the grass family, and this is the main bread grain.

clue.text: Fellow read out part of insurance document for Spanish orince

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

indicators.note: read out means said aloud, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: a car-loss section is part of a motor insurance policy

explanation.surface: A fellow reads out part of the policy covering a prince of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orince' is a typing slip for 'prince'. Don Carlos was the son of Philip II of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The son of Philip II and heir to the Spanish crown, subject of Schiller's play and Verdi's opera.

clue.text: Soon autumn comes around, time in which days darken

indicators.note: comes around means encircles, so the soon and autumn words go round the time

parts.note: nigh means near, soon
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: Autumn will soon be here, a season when the days grow dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes around' sets the time letter between soon and autumn, which together go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the hour when daylight fades into evening.

clue.text: Linesman sore after training gets new pack of ice

indicators.note: training reworks the letters, so the word sore is rearranged

parts.note: a berg is a floating mass of ice

explanation.surface: A linesman, sore from training, gets a fresh ice pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Linesman' suggests a football official, but it is a writer of lines: Isaac Rosenberg, First World War poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A poet writes lines of verse, and Isaac Rosenberg was a celebrated war poet.

clue.text: Chap who gets sacked every year by Iron City

parts.words: Chap who gets sacked every year
parts.note: Father Christmas carries a sack of presents each year
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A man who is fired annually ends up in Iron City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' suggests dismissed from work, but Father Christmas is laden with a sack each year.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of New Mexico is a US city.

clue.text: Poppy was his new chinos-wearing head of Latin

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the rearranged trousers enclose the letter
new means remade, so the letters of chinos are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A poppy was worn by a Latin teacher in new chinos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CHINOS to NICHOS; 'wearing' puts L (from 'head of Latin') inside. Poppy is Peter Nichols's play, not a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Nichols wrote the pantomime-style play Poppy, so it was his work.

clue.text: Northern town that's reported George, Harris and J?

indicators.note: reported means said aloud, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: the three rowers of Jerome's Three Men in a Boat make up a boat's crew

explanation.surface: A northern town reports on three men.
explanation.walkthrough: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewe is a town in Cheshire, north-west England.

clue.text: Horsey sort of nurse volunteers to inject dog

indicators.note: to inject is to put inside, so the nurse and volunteers go into the dog

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
EN is an enrolled nurse
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A horsey nurse and some volunteers give a dog an injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horsey sort' suggests a horse lover, but the creature is half horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature of Greek myth with a man's upper body on a horse's body.

clue.text: Philosophical bloke brought up engineers' offspring

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read upwards, so the engineers' abbreviation is turned backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
a son is offspring

explanation.surface: A thoughtful man raised the engineers' son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' looks like raising a child, but it turns REME into EMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was the American transcendentalist thinker.

clue.text: "I would send them to the Turk, to make — of" (All's Well That Ends Well)

definitions.text: "I would send them to the Turk, to make — of" (All's Well That Ends Well)

parts.words: "I would send them to the Turk, to make — of" (All's Well That Ends Well)
parts.note: Lafew's line in Shakespeare's comedy, with the word for castrated servants left blank

explanation.definitionFit: Turkish sultans kept castrated men as harem servants, which is the fate Lafew wishes on the young lords.

clue.text: Hospital screening American lady Austen knocked out!

indicators.note: screening means hiding inside, so the hospital holds the American

parts.note: a san is a sanatorium, a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital screens an American woman knocked out by Jane Austen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked out' means dashed off: Lady Susan is an early novella by Austen.
explanation.definitionFit: Austen wrote the short epistolary novel Lady Susan, so the lady she produced bears this name.

clue.text: People like Percy Alleline can be little devils

definitions.meaning: Alleline has the codename for the mender of pots in le Carre's spy novel

explanation.definitionFit: A tinker mends pots and pans; in Britain it is also slang for a naughty child.

clue.text: Animal performer mostly olagues Stubb and his ilk

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a seal is a circus animal that performs tricks
to dog someone is to plague them

explanation.surface: A performing animal pesters Stubb and others like him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'olagues' is a typing slip for 'plagues'. Stubb is the second mate in Moby-Dick.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubb is a whaling mate, and old, experienced sailors are called by this name.

clue.text: A mother with child might pick up this author

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A mother with her child may pick up a book by this author.
explanation.walkthrough: Joy Adamson wrote Born Free, about a lioness raising cubs; a dam is the word for an animal mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Joy Adamson wrote Born Free, the story of Elsa the lioness.

clue.text: Lennon's glare upset Walk on the Wild Side producer

definitions.text: Walk on the Wild Side producer

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its possessive s, all of which is used

explanation.surface: Lennon's glare upset the man who made the Walk on the Wild Side record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk on the Wild Side' suggests Lou Reed's song, but it is Algren's 1956 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Algren wrote the novel A Walk on the Wild Side, so he produced it.
